topic: Components in series and parallel; transformers (G5C; 14 pool questions)

questions.question: What causes a voltage to appear across the secondary winding of a transformer when an AC voltage source is connected across its primary winding?
What is the output voltage if an input signal is applied to the secondary winding of a 4:1 voltage step-down transformer instead of the primary winding?

choices.A: The input voltage is multiplied by 4
choices.B: The input voltage is divided by 4
choices.C: Additional resistance must be added in series with the primary to prevent overload
choices.D: Additional resistance must be added in parallel with the secondary to prevent overload

questions.answer: The input voltage is multiplied by 4

questions.question: What is the total resistance of a 10-, a 20-, and a 50-ohm resistor connected in parallel?
What is the approximate total resistance of a 100- and a 200-ohm resistor in parallel?
Why is the primary winding wire of a voltage step-up transformer usually a larger size than that of the secondary winding?

choices.A: To improve the coupling between the primary and secondary
choices.B: To accommodate the higher current of the primary
choices.C: To prevent parasitic oscillations due to resistive losses in the primary
choices.D: To ensure that the volume of the primary winding is equal to the volume of the secondary winding

questions.answer: To accommodate the higher current of the primary
